caseStudy.title: How this demo store was built
caseStudy.lead: A fictional clothing brand, a complete store, and the decisions behind it. Written for anyone judging the craft, in about two minutes.

intro.heading: What this is
intro.p1: Home Club Foundation is a made-up brand of quiet everyday essentials. The store is a demo and a portfolio project: nothing is sold, no payment is taken and no personal data is kept.
intro.p2: Products, prices and copy are fictional. The imagery is placeholder material and is not a claim about real products.

problem.heading: Problem and goals
problem.intro: The aim was to show what a careful, bilingual online store looks like when it is built the way a client would want it built. Five goals guided the work.

goals.look: Look and feel like a real, premium clothing store, on a phone and on a desktop.
goals.speed: Stay fast: Lighthouse scores of 95 or more on mobile for the home, collection and product pages.
goals.look2: Prove product logic with an Assemble your look builder that prices sets and handles stock correctly.
goals.i18n: Prove internationalisation: full Thai and English, locale-aware URLs, and prices in baht or dollars.
goals.explain: Be explainable: this page records the decisions, the trade-offs and the measured results.

constraints.heading: Constraints
constraints.intro: Six constraints shaped most of the choices below.

bilingual.title: Thai and English as equals
bilingual.body: Thai is written natively, not translated word for word. Thai text is never uppercased or letter-spaced, and it has its own line heights so that tone marks are not clipped.

money.title: One money rule
money.body: Prices are whole cents in US dollars. Baht is derived from them in a single place, at a fixed demo exchange rate that is not live data. No price is ever calculated with floating-point numbers.

static.title: Static pages with prices in the first HTML
static.body: Every page is generated ahead of time. The visitor’s currency is chosen by a hidden route segment that the proxy selects from a cookie, so pages never need to be rendered per request.

csp.title: A strict content security policy
csp.body: Scripts come from the site itself and eval is never allowed in production. Keeping pages static means inline scripts are permitted, a trade-off recorded in a decision note.

budgets.title: JavaScript budgets
budgets.body: Each route has a limit on the JavaScript it loads. The limits were rebased once on the size of the framework itself, which no application change can remove.

a11y.title: Accessibility as a release gate
a11y.body: The target is WCAG 2.2 AA. A change that adds a serious accessibility violation does not ship.

stack.heading: Stack and why
stack.intro: Each choice is the simplest tool that met the constraints. Every one is covered by a decision note in the repository.

items.next: Server Components by default, so most of the store is plain HTML and only small islands ship JavaScript.
items.typescript: Strict mode catches invalid prices, stock and routes before they reach a page.
items.tailwind: Design tokens as CSS variables keep colour, spacing and type consistent without one-off values.
items.intl: Locale-prefixed URLs, ICU messages and plurals, and typed message keys.
items.zustand: A small cart store whose saved data is checked with Zod, so stale or corrupt storage resets instead of breaking the page.
items.radix: Drawers and dialogs use a vetted primitive for focus trapping, and load only when opened.
items.vitest: Unit tests for money, stock, looks and catalogue rules, plus a check that both languages have the same message keys.
items.playwright: End-to-end journeys and an axe accessibility sweep, run against the production build.
items.lighthouse: Lighthouse CI turns the performance budgets into a check rather than a promise.

tradeoffs.heading: Trade-offs
tradeoffs.intro: Choices that cost something, stated plainly.

currency.title: The currency segment doubles the static output
currency.body: Rendering every page once per currency keeps prices in the first HTML and every page static, at the cost of twice as many generated pages.

filters.title: Filters are read in the browser
filters.body: Reading filters on the server would make collection pages dynamic. A small client island applies them instead, so the first view is always the default one.

csp.title: Inline scripts are allowed
csp.body: A per-request nonce would be stricter, but it forces every page to be rendered on demand. The policy still forbids eval and is backed by tests.

og.title: Share cards use Latin letters only
og.body: The image renderer drops some Thai tone marks, which changes the meaning of words. Share cards therefore avoid Thai text; the pages themselves are unaffected.

images.title: Placeholder and AI-generated imagery
images.body: Photographs are illustrative and some product angles are AI-generated. Each is logged with its source in the asset register and should be replaced before any public marketing use.

performance.heading: Performance evidence
performance.intro: These figures come from stored Lighthouse reports in the repository. Nothing on this page is typed in by hand.
performance.caption: Lighthouse results for {run}
performance.measured: Measured on {date}, median of {runs} mobile runs.
performance.noteLocal: Local and deployed runs differ. A local run on a slow machine under-reports speed, so the deployed result is the one that counts for the performance gate (see the decision note on JavaScript budgets).
performance.notePreview: Preview deployments are marked noindex on purpose, so the search score on a Preview is not the Production picture.
performance.gateMiss: This run missed a budget: {metric} on {route} was {actual} against a limit of {limit}.
performance.missSummary: Phase {n} missed a budget: {metric} on {route} was {actual} against a limit of {limit}. The run is listed under earlier runs.

quality.heading: Accessibility and quality

items.axe: An axe sweep runs on every route in both languages.
items.keyboard: Every feature can be used with the keyboard alone, with a visible focus ring.
items.tests: Unit tests cover the business rules, and end-to-end tests cover the main shopping journeys on a phone and a desktop viewport.

quality.screenReader: In phase 2 the owner reported a screen-reader smoke test of the look builder, search and checkout. It was done by a person, not by an automated tool.
